subject: Production braking: BrightSide latency spike + quota window mismatch
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightside.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightSide IT Ops <itops@brightside.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency spike + 503s from yesterday afternoon

Jordan —

We saw a sharp spike in latency and intermittent 503s yesterday between ~14:20–15:05 PST. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Typical p50 rose from ~120ms to 3–7s, and we observed ~1.8% 503 responses during the window.

Attached a traffic dump and a handful of request IDs (x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d, 0a1b2c3e). This is impacting our live product (search suggestions) and customers are complaining. We increased client-side retry/backoff but still saw elevated errors.

Can Redwood confirm whether this was a capacity pressure event, a routing fallback, or something on our quota/burst? We are on the Growth plan (region: us-west). This needs urgent attention — our ops and SRE teams are standing by.

Attachments: traffic_dump-2025-11-30.json

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightSide

Subject: Re: Latency spike + 503s from yesterday afternoon

Team — quick summary from initial investigation (ops):

What we saw
- Traffic pattern: concentrated on us-west, short burst pattern lasting ~45s repeated in a ~10m window (traffic_dump shows clustered bursts).
- Serving behaviour: request admission started rejecting at token-bucket exhaustion; once the bucket was depleted, subsequent requests were suppressed/fast-failed until refill increments allowed a handful through. This manifests as increased p50/p95 and a small % of 503s.

Root cause hypothesis
- BrightSide's client traffic profile has a short, high-rate burst characteristic. Their plan’s quota and our configured burst window for that account (burst_window = 60s, burst_credits = 1x baseline) don't match the incoming burst envelope. The token-bucket refill_rate was effectively throttling the peak.
- Compounding factor: regional routing favored shared hosted capacity in us-west that was operating near headroom because of unrelated scheduled jobs; that reduced our ability to absorb the transient surge.

Immediate mitigation (ops action taken)
- I applied an emergency temporary override: increased burst_credits to 3x for BrightSide (us-west) and relaxed the short-term refill constraint.
- Rerouted a portion of BrightSide traffic to a low-latency spare pool to smooth load.
- Monitors set for p50/p95 and 503 rate; alerts to on-call and to Jordan.

Customer-facing next steps
- Jordan: can you confirm with Samir that the 503s and latency reduced after ~10:55 PST? If so we'll keep the override for 24 hours while we implement a permanent fix.

Longer-term remediation (action items)
- Engineering (Marcus + Karthik): evaluate per-account burst windows and refactor token-bucket config to support short high-rate envelopes for Growth/Scale plans by Dec 8.
- Product + Sales: review plan documented burst SLAs and add guidance to onboarding.
- Ops: add include circuit-breaker backfills for scheduled jobs that consume headroom in a noisy neighbor scenario.

Attachments: redwood_quota_policy.yaml, quick-mitigation-runbook.pdf

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Looping in exec context:

We should notify CRO and CTO given customer impact and the potential for an SLA credit request. Proposed immediate steps:
- Keep the emergency override active (24h) — Laura has applied it.
- Offer BrightSide a one-time service credit for the window and expedite the quota policy alignment work. Jordan, prepare a one-line credit proposal for Samir (suggest 10% of last month’s invoice or a fixed credit — pick whichever maps to their account level).
- Marcus/Karthik: give me a short ETA for a fix that avoids manual overrides (estimate EOD Dec 8 for config change + Jan release for more robust per-account envelopes).

Please confirm we have deployment windows clear and that the low-latency pool remains stable. This needs exec visibility but I don't want to escalate to customer success leadership unless we see reoccurrence.
